To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pathologic evaluation of gastrointestinal tract carcinomas for Lynch syndrome is an important and practical tool for identifying patients at risk for the disease.
the pathologist can identify Lynch syndrome–associated tumors of the gastrointestinal system through evaluation of DNA mismatch repair protein expression.

1) the evaluation of mismatch repair protein immunohistochemistry is a reliable method for the identification of patients with Lynch syndrome; 2) the evaluation of tumors of patients with a known family history is the most efficient method for the identification and referral of patients for genetic counseling; and 3) the evaluation of patients with a personal history of colorectal carcinoma and a negative family history for Lynch syndrome is a reliable and cost-effective method for identifying patients at risk for hereditary colorectal carcinoma.

the pathologist can play a vital role in identifying patients at risk for hereditary colorectal carcinoma and can provide the information necessary for the appropriate management of patients with colorectal and other gastrointestinal tract carcinomas.
